description:
client.rs:254, 304, 382, 577 — fetch_session, call, subscribe_events, connect_ws_session

All four are async methods returning a Future. Cancellation today: drop the future. That's the Rust async cancel model and the reqwest layer handles it (dropping the response future closes the underlying connection).

But there is no graceful shutdown signal. A caller who has issued a long-running call() (say a Mailbox/changes returning 50MB of data) and wants to cancel cleanly — releasing connection-pool slot, notifying server politely — has only the drop-the-future option. Drop happens synchronously inside whatever runtime; if the future was suspended at .await inside reqwest, the cancellation propagates by reqwest closing the underlying TcpStream. That works but is abrupt.

For long-running streams (subscribe_events, the WsSession::next_frame loop), cancel semantics are even less clear:
  - tokio::select! { _ = stream.next() => ..., _ = shutdown_rx => break }
  - drops the .next() future, which drops the BoxStream's state, which drops the underlying reqwest stream.

A modern async API offers an explicit cancel token (CancellationToken, tokio_util) — pass it in at construction or per-call, the future polls it, the future returns cleanly with Err(Cancelled). The current API provides no such facility.

This is a contract underspecification: the cancel-via-drop semantic works today but isn't documented as the supported model. A caller who later wants graceful shutdown has no API support.

Low priority because (a) drop-cancel is the idiomatic Rust async model, (b) workspace policy ties cancellation to the consumer's runtime choice rather than to the foundation crate. Documentation fix would be sufficient: a Gotchas section entry: "Cancellation is via drop-future. There is no explicit cancel token; if you need graceful shutdown, wrap the future in tokio::select! against your shutdown signal."
title: JmapClient methods cannot be canceled mid-flight — no built-in cancel-token or abort handle
